correctness.rationale: Matrix-unit multiplication gives the three stated centralizer equations. With d nonzero the first and third simple-root coordinates are fixed by D, leaving an abelian kernel, of dimension three unless a=f=0, when it has dimension four. With d=0 and (a,f) nonzero, D=0 and the other equation cuts out a symplectic orthogonal hyperplane in the four noncentral coordinates; the restricted alternating form has rank two in every characteristic. With a=d=f=0 and (b,e) nonzero, the hyperplane is spanned by T=bE12+eE34 and the four-dimensional abelian ideal spanned by E23,E13,E24,E14. On that ideal ad_T has rank two; its square sends E23 to -2be E14 and is zero on the other generators. Thus the nilpotent operator has Jordan blocks (2,2) when 2be=0 and (3,1) otherwise, giving exactly the two listed Lie types over k. X itself has ad_X of rank one and square zero in both cases. Zero b and e in the last stratum leaves exactly the q central elements. Counting the disjoint coordinate cases gives the stated multiplicities and their sum q^6. An independent brute-force commuting-pair replay, factoring out the known central line and taking spans by scalar closure, confirmed all lower-central signatures over F2, F3 and F4: python3 /workspace/reproduce_3.py, output /workspace/reproduce_3.txt. The all-field Lie-isomorphism conclusion comes from the structural argument, not the signatures checked at three field orders.

Goodwin–Röhrle give Borel representatives and commuting-variety components in algebraically closed characteristic zero. Soffer studies conjugacy-class counts for unitriangular groups.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The orbit equations can organize point counts, and brackets can be evaluated at representatives. The orbit theorem is not an abstract Lie-type classification, and its field hypothesis does not supply rational conjugacy or descent by itself. In particular the three named orbits still remain separate in characteristic two in the table, which does not say that their centralizers coalesce by Lie type.

evidence: The embedded record gives the actual hyperplane row (-e,0,0,0,b) for a=d=f=0; its parametrization by [b:e] is genuine structural coverage.

One has to restrict the bracket to that hyperplane: ad_T on its abelian ideal has rank two but square proportional to -2be. Thus projective coordinate-axis points, non-axis points and the field characteristic affect the abstract classification even though rank, dimension and embedded fibre counts alone cannot separate them.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The rowspaces provide inputs for a derivation, not a published classification of their brackets. Multiplying embedded-fibre counts cannot produce the Lie multiplicities without the additional bracket analysis and identifying which kernels have the same Lie type. The available Borel table is also a route to the result, not a finite-field theorem implying the characteristic-dependent merger without this further step.

evidence: For the algebra group 1+N, C_{1+N}(1+X)=1+C_N(X), since the group factors commute exactly when XY=YX. Equality of the resulting embedded subgroups is thus equality of the embedded kernels.

Anil Kumar–Prajapati classify such equality on the d=0, af nonzero subcase into q^2(q-1) fibres with q(q-1) elements per fibre. Bhunia treats conjugacy of group centralizers in the invertible triangular group over an infinite field in characteristic other than two.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The algebra-group correspondence gives real overlap for the embedded kernels on that subcase; it does not identify all fibres producing abstractly isomorphic Lie algebras. originality.rationale: The distinct contribution is the bracket-level element census, especially the characteristic-dependent splitting within one adjoint Jordan stratum. Dimension rows and their totals are not distinct from the embedded spectrum; the commuting equations and much of the coordinate organization are also available there. The examined structural classifications make the calculation possible, but do not give the internal Lie-type equivalences or characteristic-two fusion. Passing is limited to the bracket-level classification and its type multiplicities, not a priority claim for rank or kernel counts.
residual_risks: The embedded-kernel parametrizations and explicit Borel orbit equations are close. A separate specialist computation could have already evaluated their internal Lie types.

value.rationale: In the natural smallest strictly triangular matrix Lie algebra with a class-three bracket, dimensions and adjoint Jordan type leave open a concrete internal-structure question. The exact census resolves it: two nonisomorphic five-dimensional types coexist under the same odd-characteristic adjoint Jordan data and become one type in characteristic two. The abundance and loss of the class-three type are not consequences of merely knowing the distribution by dimensions. This makes the small census a useful finite-field structural benchmark rather than a duplicate of rank data.
